summary: assign scripts python code to application workstream ownedPaths

delivery.outcome: Add scripts/**/*.py to coordination.workstreams.application.ownedPaths in .governance/manifest.json so the Python utility code under scripts/ is owned by the application workstream. This remediates GOV-WORKSTREAM-003: the code2llm-discovered planfile ticket scoped to scripts/sync-vscode-plugin-version.py (PLF-041, Shotgun Surgery: content) could not be allocated to a workstream because no ownedPaths pattern covered that file. Governance keeps scripts/publish-local-onedev-validator.sh and infrastructure keeps scripts/docker-ide-matrix.sh; the new Python-only glob never matches a .sh file, so rejectActiveScopeOverlap remains satisfied.
nonGoals: No ownership change for the individually-owned shell scripts (scripts/publish-local-onedev-validator.sh under governance, scripts/docker-ide-matrix.sh under infrastructure)
No source, test or behaviour change inside scripts/ itself
No changes to other workstreams' ownedPaths or to coordination settings other than the application list

architecture.decision: Add the single glob scripts/**/*.py to the application workstream ownedPaths list in .governance/manifest.json, placed with the other code-root globs after services/**/*.py. The glob matches Python files under scripts/ at any depth and never matches the two individually-owned .sh scripts, so application, governance and infrastructure ownership of scripts/ stays disjoint under the gate's pattern_covered_by predicate. .governance/manifest.json is not digest-pinned by .governance/manifest.lock.json (only manifest.base.json is), so no lock refresh is required.
dataChanges: application workstream now owns scripts/**/*.py; scripts Python code previously matched no workstream and triggered GOV-WORKSTREAM-003 on ticket allocation
architecture.rollback: Revert the ticket commit; application.ownedPaths returns to the previous globs and scripts Python code is unowned again.

commands: python3 -c "import json,sys;sys.path.insert(0,'.governance');from governance_check import pattern_covered_by;m=json.load(open('.governance/manifest.json'));ws=m['coordination']['workstreams'];app=ws['application']['ownedPaths'];gov=ws['governance']['ownedPaths'];inf=ws['infrastructure']['ownedPaths'];assert 'scripts/**/*.py' in app;assert any(pattern_covered_by('scripts/sync-vscode-plugin-version.py', p) for p in app);assert not any(pattern_covered_by('scripts/sync-vscode-plugin-version.py', p) for p in gov+inf);assert any(pattern_covered_by('scripts/publish-local-onedev-validator.sh', p) for p in gov) and not any(pattern_covered_by('scripts/publish-local-onedev-validator.sh', p) for p in app+inf);assert any(pattern_covered_by('scripts/docker-ide-matrix.sh', p) for p in inf) and not any(pattern_covered_by('scripts/docker-ide-matrix.sh', p) for p in app+gov)"
validation.evidence: The gate ownership predicate resolves scripts/sync-vscode-plugin-version.py to application only, keeps scripts/publish-local-onedev-validator.sh with governance only and scripts/docker-ide-matrix.sh with infrastructure only, and the new glob is present in application.ownedPaths.
The governance gate reports 0 errors from the ticket worktree.
